### Nvidia's Pop Fizzles by Mid-Morning and the Shares Stand Lower at Noon, Governor Waller Puts a Half-Point Hike on December's Table, the Retailers Beat on Tariff Refunds, and Alaska's House Count Waits for Tonight

Filed as: Edition No. 60 — The Midday Watch · 2026-11-18T12:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-18-midday-watch.html

The Midday File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 Nvidia’s Pop Fizzles by Mid-Morning and the Shares Stand Lower at Noon, Governor Waller Puts a Half-Point Hike on December’s Table, the Retailers Beat on Tariff Refunds, and Alaska’s House Count Waits for Tonight

 The midday file: a chipmaker’s beat that the market bought before the bell and sold after it; a governor of the Federal Reserve who wants December’s hike at twice the size the market has priced; three retailers whose good quarters all carry the same refund inside them; a senator who will not concede before certification and a House seat that will not be counted until tonight; two presidents opening a summit against protectionism and sanctions before the third lands; and one ship in the strait where the morning file had printed two statements side by side.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1200 ET, Wednesday, November 18, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 59, the Morning Watch, collected at 1006 today, from Edition No. 58, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 on Tuesday, from Edition No. 57, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 on Tuesday, and from Edition No. 56, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Monday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the midday figures differ from the figures those editions carried, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Midday in Brief: A Pop That Fizzled, a Half-Point on the Table, and a Count Set for Tonight

The midday’s corrections run against the morning’s direction in the markets and with it everywhere else. Nvidia’s shares, up 3.11 percent before the bell on the $115.8 billion quarter the morning file carried, stood at $154.72 and down 0.48 percent at 1000 Eastern in the 1000 account filed below, and at $152.80 and down 1.71 percent at 1054 in the quote account filed below, against Tuesday’s close of $155.46. The Dow stood down 238.98 points at 1000 while the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq stood higher in the same account; a second reading put all three lower, and both stand in the Cocked Hat. Governor Waller told CNBC that a half-point rate hike is “probably” needed at the December 8 and 9 meeting, in the same account, against a quarter-point hike priced at 92 to 95.7 percent in the minutes account filed below; the October minutes publish at 1400. Target, Lowe’s and TJX each beat the estimates in the morning’s reports, and each beat carries a tariff refund inside it, in the accounts filed below. In Alaska, Senator Sullivan’s campaign said he will not concede at least until the race is certified on November 25, in the live account filed below, and the state’s House tabulation runs at 1700 Alaska time tonight. In Shenzhen, Presidents Xi and Putin opened the APEC summit against protectionism and sanctions before the President landed, in the wire account filed below. The desk takes the files in that order.

What the midday settled is the market’s first verdict on the quarter—it is a sale, not a rally—and the size of the argument December now carries. What it left open is the rest of the file: the minutes at 1400, the tabulation tonight, the pricing after the close, and the seafarer still missing in the strait.

The Markets at Midday: An Open at $159.19, a High at $159.70, and a Share Price Below Tuesday’s Close by Noon

The morning file carried the futures and Asia’s answer; the midday file carries New York’s. Nvidia opened the regular session at $159.19, traded as high as $159.70 and as low as $151.60, and stood at $152.80 at 1054 Eastern, down $2.66 or 1.71 percent from Tuesday’s close of $155.46, in the quote account filed below. The 1000 account puts the share at $154.72, down 0.48 percent, after a premarket bounce of 3.11 percent on the earnings beat, and names the movement plainly: the pop fizzled. The figures behind the trade did not change at midday. Revenue of $115.84 billion against $109.10 billion expected, adjusted earnings of $2.68 a share against $2.48, and guidance of about $130 billion for the current quarter stand in both accounts as they stood in the morning file, with the halted Hopper shipments to China and the reported Securities and Exchange Commission probe carried as the overhang in the open account filed below. The wider chip file followed the premarket up and the morning down in pieces: Micron, AMD, Broadcom and Marvell all rose before the bell on the report, in the minutes account, and the neocloud names rose most.

The indexes split, and the desk prints the split as it found it. At 1000 Eastern the Dow stood at 50,520.44, down 238.98 points or 0.47 percent, while the S&P 500 stood up 0.24 percent and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.73 percent, in the 1000 account. The open account, in contract prices, put the Dow down about 0.7 percent, the S&P 500 down about 0.3 and the Nasdaq 100 down about 0.3, and recorded that Tuesday the S&P 500 lost about 1 percent with all eleven sectors down. The retail names carried the morning’s gains: TJX up 10.01 percent at 1000 in the 1000 account and up 10.20 percent at $143.09 in the quote account, and Target up 5.76 percent at 1000 against a premarket reading of up 0.3 percent in the premarket account filed below. Lowe’s stood down 5.7 percent in the same account. Gold fell: futures down 2.58 percent at $3,764.60 in the morning account filed below, with spot gold at its lowest in more than a year in the same reading. Settled: the beat was sold. Open: whether the minutes at 1400 give the sale a second reason.

The Fed at Midday: A Half-Point “Probably” Needed, a Quarter-Point Priced at 92 to 95.7 Percent, and the Minutes at 1400

The day’s official statement came before the open and it was a size, not a direction. Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC’s Squawk Box that a half-point rate hike is “probably” necessary at the December 8 and 9 meeting, unless the Federal Reserve clearly signals another hike for January, in the 1000 account and in the pre-open account filed below. The market he addressed has priced the smaller move: a quarter-point hike at 92 percent on Polymarket and 95.7 percent on CME FedWatch in the minutes account, about 95 percent in the pre-open account’s reading of the same tool. The funds rate stands at 3.75 to 4.00 percent, held on October 28 by a vote of 10 to 2, with Governors Cook and Hammack voting for a quarter-point hike, in the minutes account. The week’s other voices stand in the morning account: St. Louis President Musalem said on Tuesday that several rate increases are likely needed before spring, and New York President Williams said another hike is likely and the situation does not call for dramatic action.

The instrument that can move the pricing publishes at 1400: the minutes of the October 27 and 28 meeting, whose question, after the Governor’s remarks, is how many officials backed a faster pace in October, in the pre-open account. Governor Barr speaks at 1335, ahead of the minutes, in the minutes account. The bond market’s morning readings stand apart in the file: the ten-year yield at 5.121 percent, up almost two basis points, in the pre-open account, and at 5.092 percent, about a basis point lower, in the morning account; the two-year at 4.83 percent, up more than four, in the pre-open account. Both readings are printed in the Cocked Hat. Settled: a half-point is now said aloud by a sitting governor. Open: the minutes, at 1400, and December itself.

The Consumer at Midday: Three Beats, Three Tariff Refunds, and a Housing Print That Points Both Ways

The morning’s three retailers reported before the bell, and the midday file reads the three reports as one document. Target earned $2.65 a share against $2.05 expected, on revenue of $27.1 billion against $26.49 billion expected, with comparable sales up 5.6 percent against 3.8 expected—its best sales growth in five years, driven by a 5 percent rise in traffic while the average ticket rose 0.6 percent—in the signals account and the watch account filed below. Inside the beat stands a $301 million tariff refund, worth about $0.50 a share in the watch account; the company raised its full-year outlook, to earnings of $10.65 to $11.40 in the watch account and by 1 percent in the premarket account. Lowe’s earned $3.10 a share against $2.86 to $2.90 expected, on sales of $22.76 billion, up 9.3 percent, with comparable sales up 1.8 percent against 0.4 expected and online sales up 17.4 percent, in the same accounts; tariff refunds added $0.34 a share in the watch account and about $250 million in the signals account, and gross margin fell 124 basis points to 32.95 percent even with them. TJX earned $1.34 a share adjusted, a penny ahead in the premarket account and in line in the watch account, which also prints $1.39 unadjusted, on sales of $16.0 billion, up 6 percent, with comparable sales up 4 percent against its own plan of 2 to 3 percent, in the same accounts; it raised its full-year comparable-sales guide to 4 percent and guided its fourth quarter below the estimate. The common sentence in the three reports is the refund: strip it out, in the signals account’s arithmetic, and margins fell.

The morning’s other official print pointed in both directions at once. Housing starts rose 9.9 percent in October to an annual rate of 1.309 million, against a consensus of 1.245 to 1.25 million, while building permits fell 7.4 percent to 1.295 million, against 1.377 to 1.38 million expected, in the starts account, the wire account and the data account filed below. Single-family starts rose 4.0 percent to 864,000; single-family permits fell 8.7 percent to 772,000. The Census Bureau’s own caution stands in the starts account: the 90 percent interval on the monthly change is plus or minus 16.8 points and includes zero. The rate that prices the houses stands in the wire account: the 30-year fixed mortgage averaged 7.18 percent last week, up 120 basis points since the war began in late February, and builder sentiment in October fell to its lowest since April 2012 in the builders’ survey of Tuesday. Walmart reports Thursday, in the signals account. Settled: the consumer spent, and the refunds flattered the spending’s keepers. Open: permits, which are the forward half of the print.

Alaska at Midday: No Concession Before Certification, Two Investigations and an Appeal Standing, and a Tabulation at 1700 Alaska Time

The morning file called the Senate race; the midday file records what the call did not close. Senator Sullivan’s campaign said he will not concede at least until the race is certified, in the live account above, and the account carries the campaign’s Monday sentence whole: it will let the process run its course until every legal vote is counted and certified. Certification is targeted for November 25, in the same accounts. Ms. Peltola declared victory on Tuesday night—“We did it!” in the victory account filed below—and the count that carries her stands where the morning file left it: 144,302 votes, 50.12 percent, to 131,844, a lead of 12,458, with the Senate at 56 to 44. No new count from the Division of Elections stands in the midday file.

The court file outlives the count, as the morning file said it would. The Justice Department’s suit to block certification, dismissed by a federal judge—on November 1 in the victory account—stands on appeal in all the midday accounts; a federal criminal investigation into the recruitment of the second Mr. Sullivan and a state investigation ordered by Governor Dunleavy both stand open, in the win account filed below. The President’s words stand in the same file: the ballot’s second Sullivan called fraud, and a demand on November 10 that the second Sullivan’s votes and Mr. Heikes’s be given to the Senator, in the live account’s companion piece filed below. The arithmetic the morning file printed answers the demand without the desk’s help: hand the Senator every other vote in the race and he finishes 708 behind.

The state’s House seat is tonight’s fact, and midday is too early for it—the desk prints the hour so the record shows it waited. The Division of Elections runs its official ranked-choice tabulation at 1700 Alaska time, 2100 Eastern, and will livestream it, in the ballots account filed below. The unofficial tallies of the cast vote record converge on the same name at slightly different widths: Mr. Begich ahead in the final round by 7,478 votes, 51.4 to 48.6 percent, on the ballots account’s updated figures, and by 7,967 to 7,998 votes, 51.5 to 48.5, on the November 16 record in the results account filed below, which concludes there is no path for Mr. Hill on the ballots remaining. First choices stand at 137,874 for Mr. Begich and 121,143 for Mr. Hill in the updated model, and at 136,215 to 119,689 in the Alaska account filed below. Settled: the Senate, and the loser’s timetable—certification, not concession. Open: the House seat, at 2100 Eastern.

Shenzhen at Midday: Free Trade From the Host, Sanctions From the Guest, a Fifth Meeting of the Two, and a Photograph of the Three

The summit opened on Wednesday in Shenzhen before its third principal arrived, and the opening words from the two men already there pointed at the same target from their two capitals. President Xi pledged to stand up against trade protectionism and urged the region’s economies to defend free and open trade and the rules-based system centred on the World Trade Organization, in the wire account above and in the opening account filed below; President Putin criticised Western sanctions in his own address and said he expected big potential benefit from Thursday’s three-way meeting, in the same accounts. The two then met on Wednesday, their fifth meeting this year, with the Chinese readout emphasising the durability of the relationship and the carrying-out of commitments already reached, and Mr. Xi placing the meeting at the thirtieth anniversary of the two countries’ strategic partnership, in the bilateral account filed below.

The President landed after the speeches, to the welcome the morning file carried—President Xi on the tarmac in person, the first such greeting of his tenure in the wire’s reading—and the three presidents were photographed together at Wednesday night’s welcome banquet in Shenzhen, Mr. Putin walking over to shake the President’s hand as Mr. Xi received him, in the banquet account filed below. The White House’s Wednesday, as the morning file carried it, held meetings with President Sheinbaum of Mexico and Prime Minister Carney of Canada before the greeting ceremony. Thursday’s order gained one piece of furniture at midday: the President and Mr. Xi hold a working lunch first, their third face-to-face meeting this year in the opening account’s count and their fourth encounter of the year in the Paris account filed below, and the first trilateral of the three follows, at a state villa north of the city in the same account. The subjects stand as the file has carried them all week: Ukraine and Iran in the President’s words, nuclear arms in his officials’, trade and artificial intelligence in the summit’s own papers, and world peace and strategic stability in Beijing’s confirmation. Settled: the opening positions, said aloud in the host’s hall. Open: the lunch and the trilateral, on Thursday.

The Gulf at Midday: One Ship Where the Morning Printed Two Statements, Eleven Injured Against Two in Hospital, and a Search Continuing

The morning file printed two statements side by side and left the identity of the ship between them unresolved. The midday accounts join them. The shipping account filed below states that the Tara Gas is operated by ADNOC Logistics and Services, the operator whose Wednesday statement reported one crew member missing and eleven injured on an unnamed vessel; the wire account filed below carries the two statements in one story—the operator’s, and Oman’s emergency authorities’ report that they rescued 24 crew members from the Panama-flagged Tara Gas while the search continued for one missing person. The databases’ entries stand in the wire account as they stand: the ship listed under the ownership of a Marshall Islands company and the management of an Emirates-based firm. The desk prints the join as the accounts make it: one ship, the Tara Gas, struck twice—first on Monday about seven nautical miles north of Khasab in the British agency’s report, and again on Tuesday, when the crew of 25 abandoned her—and now drifting about 4.5 nautical miles southwest of Jazirat Um Alganam in the navigational warning of November 17 carried in the shipping account.

The injury count did not join. Eleven injured stands in the operator’s statement in both accounts; two injured taken to hospital stands in the Indian authorities’ figures in the shipping account, with 21 Indian seafarers brought ashore at Khasab of the 24 rescued. Both counts are printed in the Cocked Hat, unblended. The search for the one missing seafarer continued at midday in every account the desk read; no account carries his name. On the Bahrain radar, the file gains nothing for a fifth day: no assessment of the machine from any capital stands in the midday file, and the desk records the silence as a silence. Settled: the ship has one name in the midday file, and one operator. Open: the injured count, the missing man, and the radar.

The Air File at Midday: The Router Model Disabled in the Wire’s Wednesday Account, No Second Stop, and a Weather Stop at Fort Lauderdale

Wednesday’s air file is a local file, and the midday desk prints it at its size. The wire’s Wednesday account, filed below, carries the agency’s action whole: the Federal Aviation Administration has suspended installation of new network routers, technicians have linked Friday’s nationwide disruption to the recently installed Juniper router at El Dorado, Arkansas, and the agency has disabled the previously installed routers of the model while investigators examine the problem, which reached communications and radar systems at 17 of the 22 regional centres. United States officials said there is no evidence connecting Friday’s failure to the week’s other technology disruptions or suggesting malicious activity, in the same account. No second nationwide stop stands in any account the desk read.

The day’s one stop was weather’s. A ground stop for Fort Lauderdale, issued at 0833 Eastern for thunderstorms and set to run to 0945, held flights bound there at their origins, in the stop account filed below. The trackers’ national counts stand apart and are printed apart: one ground stop, one ground delay program and one airport closure across three airports in the tracker account filed below, against its own airport pages recording no widespread cancellation wave and the San Francisco disruption eased with no active programs. The Thanksgiving assurance from the Secretary stands where the morning file left it. Settled: the model is disabled and the installs are paused, now in the wire’s own Wednesday telling. Open: the root cause, which no account names.

France and Spain at Midday: A Quiet Wednesday in Paris Between a Strike and a Senate, and a Sixth Tracking in Madrid

France’s Wednesday is the interval between its facts: Tuesday’s strike day, counted in the morning file at 3.14 percent of the Education Ministry’s staff, behind it; the police bill in the Senate on Thursday, the roundabout and toll-booth occupations called for Friday to Sunday, and a sixth Saturday of marches on November 21 ahead of it. No new French figure stands in the midday file, and the desk prints the interval as an interval.

Spain’s campaign published its sixth daily reading on Wednesday, and the midday file corrects the morning file’s numbering in the open: the instalment the morning edition carried as the fifth is the sixth, on fieldwork of November 13 to 17. It puts the Popular Party at 32.2 percent and 131 seats, the Socialists at 30.7 percent and 122 seats, and Vox at 17.0 percent and 55 seats—Vox’s lowest reading of the campaign, down three seats on the day and nine from its first projection, with the Popular Party and the Socialists both gaining at its expense, in the survey account and the youth account filed below. The two right parties together hold 186 seats, or 188 counting the two Navarre seats of the Popular Party’s coalition there, against 176 needed, in the same accounts. The average of the institutes moved a tenth: the Popular Party at 31.4 percent, the Socialists at 27.4 and Vox at 19.0 across 17 institutes in the average account filed below, whose seat table prints the Popular Party at 128 and the pair at 194. Thursday carries the campaign’s single head-to-head debate; polls may publish until November 23; Spain votes November 29.

The Afternoon Ahead: Minutes at 1400, a Pricing After the Close, and a Tabulation at 2100 Eastern

The afternoon carries the October minutes at 1400, Governor Barr at 1335 ahead of them, Palo Alto Networks after the close, and October pending home sales later in the day in the starts account. After the close, Anthropic prices its offering. The terms did not move at midday: the range stands at $70 to $78 on 825 million shares in Amendment No. 3 of November 17, no pricing filing had appeared by early afternoon in London, and the reports of an expectation above $80 stand as reports, in the pricing account filed below; orders at nearly seven times the shares available stand in the morning file’s accounts and in the debut account filed below. Trading begins Thursday under the ticker ANT. Thursday also carries the President’s lunch with Mr. Xi and the first trilateral in Shenzhen, Spain’s debate, the police bill in the French Senate, and Walmart’s report. Tonight carries Alaska’s tabulation at 2100 Eastern. Alaska certifies on November 25, the day the Treasury Secretary’s ten days also run to. The Federal Reserve decides December 8 and 9; government funding runs out after December 11. The Evening Watch collects at 1800.

The Cocked Hat

Where the midday’s bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On the indexes: the Dow down 0.47 percent with the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq higher at 1000 in the 1000 account, and all three lower in the open account’s contract prices. On Nvidia: up 3.11 percent before the bell, up 3.7 in one futures account and 3.96 at 0508 in another, down 0.48 percent at $154.72 at 1000, and down 1.71 percent at $152.80 at 1054, with the morning file’s after-hours readings of 2 to 3, about 4 and 4.7 percent standing behind them. On TJX: earnings of $1.34 adjusted in both earnings accounts, $1.39 unadjusted in one, and a share rise of 10.01 percent at 1000 against 10.20 in the quote account. On Target: a full-year outlook raised by 1 percent in one account and to $10.65–$11.40 in another. On the ten-year yield: 5.121 percent and up in the pre-open account, 5.092 and down in the morning account. On December: a quarter-point hike at 92 percent, at 95 percent and at 95.7 in the three readings, and a half-point “probably” needed in a governor’s. On housing: September starts revised to 1.191 million in two accounts and printed at 1.221 million prior in a third. On Alaska’s House: a final-round lead of 7,478 votes in the updated model, 7,967 and 7,998 in the November 16 record’s two printings. On the strait: eleven injured in the operator’s statement and two in hospital in the authorities’, one ship in the midday accounts where the morning file printed two statements unjoined. On the air: one stop, one delay program and one closure in the tracker’s national count, and no active programs at the airports its own pages name hardest hit. On Spain: the Popular Party at 131 seats in the survey’s own table, 133 counting Navarre in its companion account, and 128 in the average’s; the right’s pair at 186, 188 and 194 in the same three instruments. Inside the triangle is where the week honestly stands, and the log turns on it.

 The Clippings Filed With This Edition

 Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. Thirty-four items.

 

 SubjectiveFirst Feed News — Market Watch 10 AM Update: Nvidia’s Pop Fizzles, Dow Slips 239 at the Open; TJX Jumps 10%The account carries the session at 1000 Eastern: the Dow at 50,520.44, down 238.98 points or 0.47 percent, the S&P 500 up 0.24 percent and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.73 percent; Nvidia at $154.72, down 0.48 percent, after a 3.11 percent premarket bounce on its earnings beat; TJX up 10.01 percent and Target up 5.76 percent after their results; Governor Waller’s statement to CNBC that a half-point hike is probably needed in December; and the October minutes due at 1400.

 SubjectiveValcore News — Peltola Wins Alaska Senate Seat, First Alaska Native SenatorThe account carries the call on Tuesday’s count at 50.1 percent of first choices; the campaign’s position that it will wait for certification on November 25; the open court and investigation files, the Justice Department’s appeal and the federal and state criminal investigations; and the House seat, where Mr. Begich leads, still uncalled.

 SubjectiveThe Daily BS — Democrats’ ‘Decoy Dan’ Dirty Trick Ends With a Senate Victory in Deep-Red AlaskaThe account carries the result and the dispute in its own framing: the second Sullivan below 5,000 votes against a margin above 12,000; Ms. Peltola’s victory message, “We did it!”; the spokesman’s statement that Alaskans deserve a complete and accurate count and the certification process should run its course; the federal judge’s dismissal of the suit on November 1 and the appeal; and the investigation standing open.

 SubjectiveFairVote — Preliminary Ranked Choice Voting Results in Alaska’s 2026 ElectionsThe account carries the unofficial tallies from the Division’s cast vote record of November 16, covering 285,439 ballots at an estimated 98 percent counted: in the House race Mr. Begich at 47.6 percent of first choices to Mr. Hill’s 41.7, and ahead 51.5 to 48.5 percent in the ranked-choice tally, by 7,967 votes, with the conclusion that he will win the seat.

 SubjectiveFairVote — How Will Remaining Ballots Affect Alaska’s Statewide Elections?The account carries the official tabulation’s hour—the Division livestreams its ranked-choice tallies at 1700 Alaska time on November 18—and the updated model on the current results: Mr. Begich ahead in the final round 51.4 to 48.6 percent, by 7,478 votes, on first choices of 137,874 to 121,143 with Mr. Hafner at 23,034 and Mr. McDermott at 7,682, and its finding that on the ballots counted there is no path for Mr. Hill.

 SubjectiveThe Alaska Story — Peltola Tops 50% in Alaska’s US Senate RaceThe account carries Tuesday’s update in the state’s figures: Ms. Peltola past 50 percent of first choices; and in the House race Mr. Begich at 136,215 first-choice votes, 47.54 percent, to Mr. Hill’s 119,689, 41.77 percent, a lead of 16,526 after Mr. Hill gained 323 in the update, with Mr. Hafner at 22,669 and Mr. McDermott at 7,533; the tabulation on Wednesday and certification on November 25.

 SubjectiveReuters, carried by SRN News — Xi, Putin Blast Western ‘Protectionism’ and Sanctions as Trump Lands in ChinaThe wire account, datelined Shenzhen, November 18, carries the summit’s opening: President Xi’s pledge to stand up against trade protectionism and President Putin’s criticism of Western sanctions, delivered hours before the President landed; Mr. Xi greeting the President at the airport, the first such greeting of his presidency in the account; the group photograph and banquet to follow; and Thursday’s meeting of the three, with Ukraine, Iran, trade, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons among its expected subjects.

 SubjectiveAsiaToday — APEC Shenzhen Summit Opens as Xi Urges Free TradeThe account carries the opening of the 33rd Economic Leaders’ Meeting: President Xi urging the region to defend free and open trade, the rules-based system centred on the World Trade Organization, and the smooth running of supply chains, under the theme of building an Asia-Pacific community that prospers together; President Putin’s expectation of big potential benefit from Thursday’s meeting; the working lunch of the President and Mr. Xi ahead of the trilateral; and the banquet on Wednesday evening with the working sessions on Thursday.

 SubjectiveThe American Quorum — Xi and Putin Meet in Shenzhen Ahead of Three-Way Talks With TrumpThe account carries Wednesday’s bilateral: the Chinese readout’s emphasis on the durability of the relationship and the carrying-out of commitments; Mr. Xi’s placing of the meeting at the thirtieth anniversary of the strategic partnership; President Putin’s statement to the business summit audience that he expected potential benefits from the three-way meeting; and Beijing’s confirmation of Thursday without a detailed agenda.

 SubjectiveLe Monde — With Trump and Putin at His Side, Xi Puts Himself Front and Center on World StageThe account carries the summit in the paper’s framing: the fourth encounter of the Chinese and American leaders in a single year; the President the first to travel to China twice in one year; Wednesday’s speech and banquet in central Shenzhen and Thursday’s meetings at a state villa in the hills north of the city; and the Canadian, Australian and Mexican leaders among about twenty expected.

 SubjectiveBrussels Signal — Trump Lands in China for First Three-Way Summit With Xi and PutinThe account carries the arrival and the evening: the three presidents together at the welcome banquet of the 33rd Economic Leaders’ Meeting at the Shenzhen International Communication Centre on November 18, in its photograph’s caption; the greeting with a hug at the airport, returning the gesture of September; Mr. Xi’s talks with Mr. Putin the same day, their fifth meeting this year; and the trilateral set for November 19.

 SubjectiveReuters, carried by WBOW — UAE’s ADNOC L&S Says One Crew Member Missing After Attack on Its Vessel in HormuzThe wire account carries the two statements in one story: the operator’s, that one crew member is missing and eleven injured after its vessel was attacked on Tuesday, the rest evacuated, the vessel unnamed; and Oman’s emergency authorities’, that they rescued 24 crew members from the Panama-flagged Tara Gas while the search continued for one missing person; the maritime sources’ account of the crew abandoning ship after a projectile strike; and the database entries listing the ship under a Marshall Islands owner and an Emirates-based manager.

 SubjectiveMaritime Telegraph — LPG Tanker Tara Gas Hit Twice in Strait of Hormuz, One Seafarer MissingThe account carries the ship’s two strikes and names her operator as ADNOC Logistics and Services: the first attack on November 16 about seven nautical miles north of Khasab in the British agency’s report, the second on November 17 firing the ship and forcing the abandonment off the Musandam Peninsula; 24 of 25 crew rescued, 21 Indian seafarers ashore at Khasab and two injured in hospital in the Indian authorities’ figures, against eleven injured in the operator’s; the ship drifting about 4.5 nautical miles southwest of Jazirat Um Alganam in the November 17 navigational warning; and the search continuing.

 SubjectiveAssociated Press, carried by NewsTalk 98.9 — FAA Grounds New Router Installations After Nationwide Flight DisruptionsThe wire account carries the agency’s Wednesday position: installation of new network routers suspended; Friday’s disruption linked by technicians to the recently installed Juniper router at El Dorado, Arkansas; the previously installed routers of the model disabled while investigators examine the problem; the failure’s reach to communications and radar at 17 of the 22 regional centres; and officials’ statement that there is no evidence connecting the incidents or suggesting malicious activity.

 SubjectiveCockpit Radar — Ground Stop Issued for Fort Lauderdale Due to ThunderstormsThe account carries Wednesday’s one stop: flights bound for Fort Lauderdale held at their origins from 0833 Eastern for thunderstorms, the stop set to run to 0945 and liable to change, in the agency’s recorded positions and public data.

 SubjectiveInvezz — Anthropic Set to Price IPO Tonight, Reports Point Above $80The account carries the pricing night’s state: the offering still marketed at $70 to $78 in Amendment No. 3 of November 17, on 825 million shares; the Journal’s report of an expectation above $80; the separate $26 billion placement closing at the same price; no pricing filing on the register by early afternoon in London; and trading scheduled for Thursday under the ticker ANT.

### Alaska Is Called for Ms. Peltola at 50.12 Percent and the Senate Stands 56 to 44, Nvidia Reports $115.8 Billion and Guides to $130 Billion With No Return for Mr. Huang, and the President Lands in Shenzhen to a Tarmac Welcome From President Xi

Filed as: Edition No. 59 — The Morning Watch · 2026-11-18T10:06:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-18-morning-watch.html

The Morning File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 Alaska Is Called for Ms. Peltola at 50.12 Percent and the Senate Stands 56 to 44, Nvidia Reports $115.8 Billion and Guides to $130 Billion With No Return for Mr. Huang, and the President Lands in Shenzhen to a Tarmac Welcome From President Xi

 The morning file: the last Senate race of the midterms is called in Alaska on Tuesday night’s count, two weeks after Election Day; Nvidia’s first report without its founder beats every estimate in the file and guides the next quarter to $130 billion; Asia buys back two days of selling; the four Quad leaders warn on coercion in Manila without naming its object; President Xi meets Air Force One on the Shenzhen tarmac while President Putin is met by an aide; two ships are named in the strait and a seafarer is missing; the Federal Aviation Administration disables the router model at the centre of Friday’s stop and says it does not know the cause; and the hemisphere’s measles map is redrawn, with the United States endemic for the first time since 2000.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1006 ET, Wednesday, November 18, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 58, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 on Tuesday, from Edition No. 57, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 on Tuesday, and from Edition No. 56, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Monday. The desk filed no Midnight Watch and no Overnight Watch for today; the gap stands in the log as a gap, and the file resumes with this watch. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where this morning’s figures differ from the earlier figures, the difference is stated here, in the open.

 The Morning in Brief: A Senate Called, a Quarter Priced, and a President Landed

 The morning calls the last Senate race, prices the chipmaker’s quarter, and lands the President in Shenzhen. The Press called Alaska’s Senate race for Ms. Peltola at 10:19 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday, on a count of 144,302 votes to 131,844 — 50.12 percent of first choices, past the majority line, so the ranked-choice tabulation set for today will not be run for the Senate; the Senate of the 120th Congress stands 56 to 44. Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the quarter ended October 25, up 103 percent on the year, and guided the current quarter to $130 billion, in the results account filed below; Asia’s Wednesday session bought the chip stocks back, Seoul closing up 2.0 percent. The Quad’s leaders, meeting in Manila on Tuesday, warned against economic coercion in a statement that named no country, in the Manila account filed below. The President landed in Shenzhen on Wednesday afternoon, China time, and was met on the tarmac by President Xi in person, in the arrival account filed below; President Putin, arrived earlier, was met by an aide. In the strait, a gas carrier abandoned off Oman has a seafarer missing, and an Emirati operator counts eleven injured on a second vessel. The desk takes the files in that order.

 What the morning settled is the Senate, the quarter, and the order of the Shenzhen week — Manila on Tuesday, the arrival today, the bilateral and the first trilateral on Thursday. What it left open is the rest of the file: the House tabulation in Juneau, the cause of Friday’s stop, the price of the Anthropic listing tonight, and whether the strait’s missing seafarer is found.

 Alaska, at 1006: 144,302 to 131,844, Past the Line on the First Count, and the House to a Tabulation

 Alaska’s count ended on Tuesday night, two weeks after Election Day, and it ended on the first count. The Division of Elections’ Tuesday evening count, with all 401 precincts reporting and 290,003 ballots cast, stands at 144,302 votes for Ms. Peltola, 50.12 percent, to 131,844, 45.80 percent, for Senator Sullivan — a lead of 12,458 — with Mr. Heikes at 6,105, Mr. Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. at 4,760 and 885 write-ins, in the call account filed below. The Press called the race for Ms. Peltola at 10:19 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday and NBC News projected her the winner the same night, in the same account. Because she cleared half of the first-choice votes, the ranked-choice tabulation scheduled for today will not be run for the Senate seat; no ballot is redistributed.

 The margin answers the file’s longest-running question by itself. Hand the Senator every vote cast for the other Mr. Sullivan, every vote for Mr. Heikes and every write-in, and he would still finish 708 votes behind Ms. Peltola, in the call account — the arithmetic that the recruitment case, in which a retired teacher of the Senator’s surname was alleged to have been recruited to divide the vote, will now be argued against in the courts; the Justice Department is appealing a dismissal and the criminal investigation remains active, in the majority account filed below. Ms. Peltola, 53, is Yup’ik and becomes the first Alaska Native to serve in the United States Senate, in the same account.

 The seat is the ninth the Democrats flipped in the midterms, the most since 1958, and it makes the Senate 56 to 44, counting the two independents who caucus with the party, against the 53 to 47 the Republicans carried into the elections, in the call account. The state’s House seat stands open: Mr. Begich leads the independent Mr. Hill 47.54 percent to 41.77, short of a majority, so that race goes to the ranked-choice count today, in the same account. Overseas ballots may arrive through today; the state finishes counting today and plans to certify on November 25, in the accounts filed below. Settled: the Senate, on the first count, by 12,458 votes. Open: the House seat, in today’s tabulation, and the court file, which outlives the count.

 Nvidia, at 1006: $115.8 Billion Reported, $130 Billion Guided, and No Return for Mr. Huang

 Nvidia’s third quarter, the first reported since Mr. Huang’s resignation on November 12, beat the company’s own guidance by more than the guidance’s margin. Revenue for the quarter ended October 25 was $115.8 billion, up 20 percent on the quarter and 103 percent on the year, against the company’s outlook of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2 percent, and a consensus of about $109 billion, in the results account filed below. Data Center revenue was $107.6 billion, up 110 percent on the year and about 93 percent of the total; earnings were $2.68 a share on the adjusted basis against about $2.47 expected, and $2.70 on the reported basis, with net income of $65.3 billion, up 105 percent; gross margin was 74.8 percent reported and 74.9 adjusted, in the quarter account filed below. The filing was signed by Ms. Kress in her capacity as interim chief executive and chief financial officer, in the read-back account filed below.

 The guidance is the report’s second fact. For the current quarter the company expects revenue of $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3 percent, against a consensus near $125 billion, with gross margin of 71 to 72 percent, in a 14-week quarter that includes an extra week, and on the stated assumption of no data-center compute revenue from China, in the quarter account. Ms. Kress raised the outlook for fiscal 2028 growth to about 75 percent, from about 70, and put the cloud industry’s revenue backlog at roughly $2.5 trillion, up from about $2 trillion a quarter ago, in the same account. The chief financial officer’s commentary carries the supply file forward: supply commitments rose from $279 billion last quarter to $390 billion, primarily for multi-year procurement of memory supply, in the read-back account. The board added $150 billion to the buyback authorization in September, leaving about $227.3 billion available, in the quarter account.

 The leadership question gained its plainest sentence in the earnings coverage: the board said it will not reinstate Mr. Huang and is searching for a permanent successor, in the quarter account. Monday’s file had the board’s position at three removes: reported not weighing a return, and not in talks, by a person familiar with the matter. The shares rose in extended trading on Tuesday evening — by 2 to 3 percent in one account, about 4 in another and 4.7 in a third; all three readings stand in the cocked hat. The quarter itself predates the resignation: the numbers show the company Mr. Huang ran, and the guidance the one Ms. Kress runs. No finding has been made by the board, by any committee or by any court on any allegation in the leadership file.

 The Markets, at 1006: Seoul Back Above 5,000, Hong Kong Down on JD.com, and the Consumer at Plus 0.2

 Asia’s Wednesday session took the report as its instruction and bought the chipmakers back, unevenly. Seoul’s Kospi rose 1.99 percent to 5,067.44, recovering much of Tuesday’s 2.6 percent fall and closing back above 5,000, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix up between 2 and 4 percent, in the close account filed below. Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.28 percent to 59,024.28, its first gain in three sessions, after rising more than 700 points at the open and dipping negative on uncertainty over American rules for AI data centres; Advantest rose 4.56 percent and SoftBank Group 3.11, in the same account. Taipei’s index rose 0.26 percent to 40,194.91. Hong Kong went the other way: the Hang Seng fell 0.91 percent to 23,294.75, with JD.com down 7.18 percent after its results and Tencent down 0.85 ahead of its own, in the same account. Shanghai’s Composite rose 0.09 percent to 3,587.83.

 The American morning opened on the same instruction. Nasdaq-100 futures rose 0.61 percent and S&P 500 futures 0.25 percent in the morning’s accounts, after the S&P 500’s fourth consecutive fall on Tuesday, in the futures account filed below. Tuesday’s other American fact was the consumer: October retail and food services sales rose 0.2 percent to $748.2 billion, matching the consensus, after September’s 0.8 percent, which was left unrevised, in the Census account filed below. The detail ran stronger than the headline: sales excluding motor vehicles rose 0.6 percent, and the control group that feeds the national accounts rose about 0.6 percent against about 0.4 expected, in the retail account filed below; a bank raised its fourth-quarter growth estimate by six-tenths to a 2.4 percent annual pace on the figures, in the same account. The Census Bureau’s own caution stands in its release: the monthly change carries a margin of plus or minus 0.4 points, an interval that includes zero. Motor vehicle sales fell 1.6 percent and furniture 2.3, in the Census account. Target, Lowe’s and TJX report today, in the week’s accounts; the Federal Reserve publishes the October meeting minutes at 1400.

 Manila, at 1006: A Statement Against Coercion That Names No Country, and a Minerals Claim Without a Text

 The four leaders met in Manila on Tuesday — the President, Prime Minister Modi of India, Prime Minister Albanese of Australia and Prime Minister Takaichi of Japan — the first Quad leaders’ meeting in more than two years, the first of the President’s second term, and the first held in a country that is not a member, in the summit account filed below. Their joint statement opposed “any destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion,” and expressed “grave concerns” about “economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions,” in the statement account filed below. The statement named no country.

 The announced work is technical and maritime. An inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum will meet in early 2027; the four support the Super Intelligence Accelerator announced by their foreign ministers in Atlanta, backed by more than $85 million in the Manila paper’s account; a new Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration will share information, and in 2027 the four countries’ P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft will fly a joint exercise for the first time under the Quad name; Australia expands its contribution to the cable partnership to electricity cables and to undersea projects in the Indian Ocean; and cybersecurity cooperation is enlarged, citing the rapid increase in incidents in the region, in the statement account. The statement uses “Super Intelligence” where the other three governments say artificial intelligence, with a footnote explaining the equivalence, in the same account.

 One claim stands in the President’s words and not in the statement. At the meeting the President said the four had signed several important new critical minerals and rare earths deals to secure supply chains against coercion by any single foreign supplier, and that the United States would match China’s rare earth output within 10 months — “We’re going to catch them within 10 months” — in the minerals account filed below. No details of the agreements — minerals, companies or values — were made public, and the leaders’ joint statement did not mention critical minerals, in the same account. A separate American-Philippine technology pact will not be signed on this trip, in the statement account. The President’s Tuesday closed with the ASEAN-United States special summit and dinner in the overnight file; on Wednesday morning he was received by President Marcos Jr. at Malaca&ntilde;ang Palace for the welcome ceremony of his state visit to the Philippines, in the arrival accounts filed below. Settled: the statement, the forum, the exercise. Open: the minerals, which stand as a claim without a text.

 Shenzhen, at 1006: A Hug on the Tarmac for One President, an Aide for the Other, and Thursday’s Three Chairs

 The President landed at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport on Wednesday afternoon, China time, and President Xi came to the aircraft to meet him — a handshake at the foot of the stairs that became a hug, with dancers waving flowers and flags, an honour guard presenting arms, a band playing the two anthems and jets overhead, in the tarmac account and the Xinhua account filed below. Mr. Xi recalled that the President and the First Lady had made a special trip to meet him at the airport during his state visit to the United States in September, and the welcome reciprocated that gesture, in the Xinhua account. An American broadcaster’s reading, printed as its reading: the welcome is believed to be the first time Mr. Xi, in power for more than a decade, has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China, in the tarmac account.

 President Putin arrived earlier on Wednesday and was met by Mr. Cai Qi, a member of the Politburo Standing Committee, and not by Mr. Xi, in the tarmac account; Mr. Xi held talks with Mr. Putin in Shenzhen on Wednesday, their fifth meeting this year, in the three-way account filed below. The White House said the President would meet President Sheinbaum of Mexico and Prime Minister Carney of Canada on Wednesday before the official APEC greeting ceremony, in the arrival account. At the leaders’ introductions on Wednesday night, Mr. Putin approached the President, and the three presidents were photographed together at the welcome banquet, in the same accounts. Mr. Musk will participate in some events during the visit, his role unstated, in the tarmac account.

 Thursday carries the week’s fixed points: a bilateral between the President and Mr. Xi, expected to address the trade tensions left from last year’s tariff war, and then the first trilateral of the three presidents, at which the President says he plans to talk about limiting nuclear weapons, the war in Ukraine and the American war with Iran, in the three-way account. The wire’s framing of the arrival stands in its lede and is printed as its framing: the President seeks to reinforce the United States’ standing as the world’s leading technology power while a series of technical outages at home has left his administration scrambling to calm the public, in the arrival account. The APEC leaders’ meeting runs today and Thursday. Settled: the order of welcome, and who stood on which tarmac. Open: everything the three men will say to each other on Thursday.

 The Gulf, at 1006: The Tara Gas Abandoned, Eleven Injured on an Unnamed Ship, and No Word on the Radar for a Fourth Day

 The strait’s file gained names and a missing man. The Panama-flagged gas carrier Tara Gas, 53,200 tons, was struck twice off Oman’s Musandam Peninsula — first on Monday evening, disabling the ship and firing its engine room, and again on Tuesday, when a second strike set it ablaze and its crew of 25 abandoned it — in the shipping account filed below. Twenty-four of the crew were rescued, 21 of them Indian nationals brought ashore at Khasab; one Indian seafarer is missing and two others were injured, in the same account. The British maritime agency had reported the first attack at about seven nautical miles north of Khasab, in the overnight file and the same account.

 A second operator’s statement does not obviously describe the same ship. ADNOC Logistics and Services, the shipping arm of Abu Dhabi’s state energy company, said on Wednesday that one crew member was missing and 11 injured after one of its vessels was attacked in the strait on Tuesday, that the rest of the crew had been safely evacuated, and that search and rescue continued; the company did not name the vessel or say what struck it, in the operator account filed below. A compiled account names a second gas tanker struck on Tuesday and identifies the Tara Gas as that vessel, in the vessels account filed below; whether the ADNOC ship and the Tara Gas are one ship or two stands unresolved in the file, and the desk prints both statements as they stand. The same compiled account names the Liberia-flagged crude tanker Al Dhanna, its stern steering gear room damaged in the Gulf before reaching the strait, turned back toward Dubai. The On Phoenix, struck by an unidentified projectile while leaving the strait early on Monday, stands in the overnight file as the week’s first named ship.

 The two militaries traded fire on Tuesday on the file’s own terms. American fighter aircraft struck a Revolutionary Guards missile launch site on Qeshm Island after Guards drones targeted an American radar system at an air base in Bahrain; Central Command said the strike was self-defence, that the drones were intercepted, and that there was no damage to American equipment or personnel, in the vessels account. The Guards claimed several tankers struck naval mines on routes Tehran considers unauthorised, and claimed to have shot down an American MQ-1 Predator drone over Qeshm, the 18th such interception claimed since the war began; neither claim has been independently confirmed, in the same accounts. The Guards’ standing arithmetic — six tankers caught fire and sunk since Sunday — remains a claim without a named or confirmed ship, in the vessels account. The United Nations’ maritime agency has recorded 136 security incidents involving vessels in and around the strait between March 1 and November 11, 35 of them in October, in the same account; satellite tracking counted an average of 0.4 tankers a day through the strait in the week to November 15, against 40.4 a day before the war, in the strait account filed below. On the Bahrain radar itself — the machine at the centre of the week’s oldest open question — Central Command’s Tuesday sentence says drones targeted a radar system and were intercepted with no damage; the earlier file’s question, what Friday’s attack did to the radar at Al-Riffa, gains no assessment from any capital for a fourth day.

 The Air File, at 1006: The Router Model Disabled, the Cause Recreated but Not Found, and $4 Billion Questioned

 The cause file for Friday’s ground stop gained a mechanism and kept its mystery. The Secretary, after sitting in on the Senate Republicans’ weekly lunch on Tuesday, told reporters that investigators have recreated the failure but cannot yet say what caused it — “We do not yet have clarity on the root cause of what happened” — in the cause account filed below. The router at the centre of it was the 69th of its kind installed, after 68 others worked without problems; it began broadcasting into the network, and the agency believed its broadcasting feature had been disabled and does not know how its configuration changed, the Administrator said at the same briefing, in the same account. The failure reached communications and radar systems at 17 of the country’s 22 regional control centres, in the installations account filed below.

 The agency has acted on the machine, if not on the cause. The Federal Aviation Administration said on Tuesday it would pause installation of new routers, has suspended use of that router model, made by Juniper Networks, and has disabled units already in service while investigators examine the problem, in the cause account and the installations account. The contractor’s copper-to-fibre work at El Dorado, Arkansas, and the second site at Amarillo stand in the earlier file. No second nationwide stop stands in any account the desk read, and the Secretary said the problem has been isolated, that the airspace should operate normally through the Thanksgiving travel days, and that he would halt flights again if needed, in the cause account.

 The money argument acquired its Republican questions. The Secretary said the $12.5 billion approved last year is committed, and that the department pays contractors only when equipment is delivered; he would accept any amount Congress approves and urged the $50 billion, in the cause account. Senator Cassidy questioned the agency’s handling of the money, put the unspent figure at about $4 billion — the figure the Majority Leader used on Monday and the Democrats’ account rendered as spent or committed — and suggested an independent investigation could help determine the cause, in the funding account filed below. The President’s sentence stands in the earlier file: very, very old equipment that had a heart attack. Settled: the model is suspended and the installs are paused. Open: the root cause, which the recreation did not supply, and whether Congress pays before December 11.

 Measles, at 1006: Elimination Withdrawn From Three Countries, 5,412 Cases, and Twelve Months to Win It Back

 The hemisphere’s measles map was redrawn on Tuesday. The Pan American Health Organization’s Director, Dr. Barbosa, accepted the recommendation of its verification commission, which met from November 10 to 13, that endemic measles transmission had been reestablished in the United States, Mexico and Bolivia, and withdrew the three countries’ elimination status, in the status account filed below. The test is the same one Canada failed a year ago: the same genotype and lineage circulating without interruption for twelve months or more. The United States had held the status since 2000, Mexico since 1996.

 The counts behind the decision are the worst in a generation. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention counted 5,412 confirmed cases in the United States in 2026 through November 12, the highest annual total since 1991, across 45 states and the capital district, with more than 590 hospitalizations, and 2,289 cases in 2025 — more than 7,700 across the two years, in the status account and the decision account filed below. The region counted 58,213 confirmed cases and 82 deaths in 2026 as of November 13, in the same accounts. The deaths stand apart in the file’s readings: thirteen dead since 2025 in one account, six deaths in the CDC’s 2026 count in another; both stand in the cocked hat.

 The American answers were given the same day. The CDC’s Director, Dr. Schwartz, said the designation is not what protects Americans and that vaccination does, and that the loss would not change the agency’s approach; the Secretary, Mr. Kennedy, promised in a social media post on Tuesday that the administration will stop the outbreaks and work to regain the lost status, in the decision account. To regain it, each country must submit a corrective action plan — expected in the coming weeks — and then document twelve months without endemic transmission, in the status account. Bolivia’s Health Minister said her country’s cases had dropped 83 percent this year, crediting vaccination, tracing, border controls and community surveillance, in the setback account filed below.

 France and Spain, at 1006: A Strike Day Smaller Than Its Billing, 15,000 Detentions Counted, and a Tracking at 131 to 122 to 55

 France’s strike day came in smaller than its billing. Turnout at Tuesday’s one-day public sector strike fell sharply and the day passed largely peacefully, in the detentions account filed below; the police had expected 220,000 to 300,000 nationwide and 40,000 to 80,000 in Paris, in the strike account filed below. ### Measles in Canada, the United States, and Mexico, 2024–2026: Where the Outbreak Spread and Who It Reached

Filed as: Special Report — Filed Outside the Watches · 2026-11-18T10:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/special-reports/2026-11-18-measles-americas.html

Special Report

 Measles · Canada · United States · Mexico · Bolivia · Guatemala · Elimination Status

 Objective

 Measles in Canada, the United States, and Mexico, 2024–2026: Where the Outbreak Spread and Who It Reached

 On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization withdrew the measles elimination status of the United States, Mexico, and Bolivia, a year after Canada lost its own. The record shows one virus lineage carried along kinship and migration routes between conservative Mennonite communities in Canada, Texas, Chihuahua, and Bolivia, then outbreaks in other close-knit groups, and then spread into general populations, Indigenous communities above all in Mexico. The hemisphere has counted 58,213 confirmed cases and 82 deaths in 2026, more than half of them in Guatemala.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1000 ET, Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

The Record in Brief

The decision. On Tuesday, November 17, 2026, PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa accepted the recommendation of the organization’s regional verification commission, which met November 10 to 13, that endemic measles transmission had been reestablished in Bolivia, Mexico, and the United States, and he withdrew the three countries’ elimination status. The commission’s test is mechanical: the same genotype and lineage of the virus circulating without interruption for twelve months or more inside one country. Canada lost its status on that test on November 10, 2025, and the Americas lost theirs as a region on the same day. The United States had held the status since 2000, Mexico since 1996, and the region since 2016, with a lapse from 2018 to 2024 after outbreaks in Venezuela and Brazil.

The counts. Canada’s multijurisdictional outbreak, which began in October 2024, reached 6,417 cases across ten provinces and territories before the Public Health Agency of Canada declared it over in October 2026. The United States recorded 2,289 cases in 2025 and more than 5,400 in 2026 through mid-November, its highest count since 1991, with ten measles-associated deaths reported by states this year. Mexico’s Health Ministry counts 20,701 confirmed cases and 50 deaths across 2025 and 2026. Across the hemisphere, PAHO counted 58,213 confirmed cases and 82 deaths in 2026 as of November 13; Guatemala, with 34,748 cases and 53 deaths through October 31, accounts for the largest single share.

The pattern. PAHO reported in August 2025 that one genotype had been identified in outbreaks in eight countries, and in its words it was found “particularly among Mennonite communities.” Inside the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has documented the same tendency across a quarter century: nearly every large outbreak since 2000 has run through a close-knit, undervaccinated community. The 2025–2026 outbreaks follow that pattern at their origins and depart from it as they grow: PAHO noted in the same 2025 report that cases were increasing outside these groups, and the largest national totals, in Guatemala and Mexico, are now dominated by general and Indigenous populations.

1. The Chain: New Brunswick, Ontario, Texas, Chihuahua

The Canadian outbreak began with an imported case. Health Canada’s briefing notes trace it to an internationally acquired infection and an exposure at a wedding in New Brunswick in October 2024; Canadian reporting identifies the traveler as arriving from Thailand and the wedding as a Mennonite gathering whose guests returned to southwestern Ontario. Ontario’s chief medical officer of health, Dr. Kieran Moore, told local health units that the outbreak was disproportionately affecting Mennonite, Amish, and other Anabaptist communities, and said the vast majority of Ontario’s cases were among them. Local health units translated measles materials into Low German, the language of the Mennonite communities most affected. Alberta followed, then Manitoba, which recorded 1,038 cases from February 2025 before declaring its outbreak over on October 16, 2026. Two Canadian deaths were recorded, both premature infants infected in the womb.

The Texas outbreak, first reported on January 17, 2025, was centered in Gaines County, in a largely Mennonite community around Seminole; about 54 percent of the Texas cases were in that county, and officials believed the virus had come from the Ontario outbreak. Two unvaccinated children died in Texas and an unvaccinated adult in New Mexico. The communities involved share a documented migration history: Low German-speaking Mennonites moved from Canada to Mexico and Paraguay in the 1920s, and from Mexico to Belize, Bolivia, and West Texas in the decades after, and families visit across those borders.

That route carried the virus south. Mexican health officials trace Chihuahua’s first case to an unvaccinated Mennonite schoolboy who visited relatives in Seminole early in 2025 and fell ill after returning home; his school closed within weeks. Chihuahua sequenced more than 100 cases and every one returned genotype D8, lineage MVs/Ontario.CAN/47.24, the strain first detected in Canada in 2024 and later in Texas. By the end of 2025 the state, roughly the size of Michigan, had about 4,500 confirmed cases, more than the entire United States that year. The virus then reached agricultural laborers, many of them Indigenous, and moved through all 32 Mexican states. Mexico’s director of epidemiological information, Dr. Miguel Nakamura, has said the national epidemic traces to the Chihuahua outbreak.

2. Where It Spread: The Communities in the Record

Low German Mennonite communities in Ontario, Alberta, West Texas, Chihuahua, and Bolivia are the common ground of the outbreak’s early chain. These are conservative branches of a broad Anabaptist tradition; Mennonite practice ranges from fully modern congregations to colonies that limit technology and contact with outside institutions, and health officials in all three North American countries have described language, distance, and distrust of government as barriers alongside religious objection.

Short Creek, on the Utah–Arizona line. An outbreak that began in August 2025 in the twin towns of Hildale, Utah, and Colorado City, Arizona, a former enclave of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints that is now increasingly ex-FLDS, passed 500 cases by April 2026; the CDC linked it to the Texas outbreak. Utah’s statewide chain, which began two months earlier, in June 2025, ran to more than 600 cases by June 2026. Local officials describe a community rebuilding after the Warren Jeffs era, in which missed childhood vaccinations had not been a priority until measles arrived.

Spartanburg County, South Carolina. The largest single U.S. outbreak since elimination began in October 2025 and reached 997 cases before it was declared over on April 27, 2026. South Carolina’s Department of Public Health estimates that about 90 percent of the outbreak’s cases were in the area’s Ukrainian- and Russian-speaking community, which numbers about 15,000 people and centers on Slavic evangelical churches; exposures were traced to several Russian-language congregations, and one charter school serving the community reported a vaccination rate of 21 percent.

Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. Pennsylvania has the most U.S. cases of 2026, more than 1,350, over a third of them in Lancaster County, home to the country’s largest Amish population. The outbreak has especially affected the Plain communities of Amish and conservative Mennonites; a 2025 estimate put measles vaccination within the local Amish community at about a quarter. County officials have also stated that the outbreak is not contained to Plain communities and is centered among unvaccinated people generally. Pennsylvania has recorded its first measles deaths in 35 years; the state counted at least five by late October. Community leaders say the case count is an undercount, because many people with measles never see a doctor.

Mexico’s Indigenous communities. PAHO reported in 2025 that Indigenous communities had been hardest hit in Mexico, that most Mexican deaths were among Indigenous people aged 1 to 54, and that the case-fatality rate in those communities was about twenty times that of the general population. The 2026 Mexican epidemic is concentrated in Jalisco, with 7,290 cases this year, followed by Mexico City and Chiapas. Among roughly 7,000 Mexican patients whose vaccination status was known in early 2026, 91.2 percent had no record of vaccination.

The precedent. The last outbreak to threaten U.S. elimination status, in 2018 and 2019, ran through Orthodox Jewish communities in Brooklyn and Rockland County, New York; it began with an unvaccinated child infected in Israel, infected more than 600 people in Brooklyn, and ended after emergency vaccination orders and community-led outreach raised coverage among young children in the affected neighborhoods from under 80 percent to about 91 percent. New York repealed religious exemptions from school vaccination in June 2019. The 2025–2026 record does not place Orthodox Jewish communities among the drivers of the current outbreaks.

3. The Rest of the Hemisphere, and Beyond It

Bolivia lost its status alongside the United States and Mexico. Its outbreak began in Santa Cruz in April 2025; the Health Ministry traced the first case to a traveler arriving from Russia and the first chain of transmission to a Mennonite colony. Bolivia has more than 150 Mennonite colonies, most of them in Santa Cruz, and PAHO describes the outbreak as spreading from those colonies to isolated Indigenous communities and the general population, with more than 600 cases reported by early 2026.

Guatemala had one case in 2025 and has the hemisphere’s largest outbreak in 2026: 34,748 confirmed cases and 53 deaths through October 31, by PAHO’s bulletin of November 5. PAHO’s April situation report linked an early cluster to a Christian religious meeting and recorded spread to at least 19 of the country’s 22 departments. Two notes govern the figure. In March 2026 Guatemala stopped taking laboratory samples from epidemiologically linked cases, and in July a retrospective update added 20,078 cases confirmed by linkage, raising the national total from 7,067 to 27,145 at a stroke. Guatemala retains its elimination status; its outbreak began in 2026 and has not yet run the twelve months the test requires.

Elsewhere in the Americas, PAHO’s spring reporting recorded cases in Belize, Paraguay, Peru, El Salvador, Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Colombia, Costa Rica, Chile, Panama, and the Caribbean Netherlands, most of them imported or limited clusters; the August 2025 genotype finding named Mennonite communities in Belize, Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay among those affected. Outside the Americas, the World Health Organization confirmed early in 2026 that Armenia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Spain, the United Kingdom, and Uzbekistan had lost their elimination status, and the European Union and its neighbors reported more than 35,000 cases in 2024. The WHO counted 186,168 cases in 165 member states from January through July 2026.

4. Vaccination Coverage and the Numbers Behind It

Measles requires about 95 percent two-dose coverage in every community to stop sustained spread; the CDC puts two doses of the MMR vaccine at about 97 percent effective. National averages conceal the gaps the outbreaks found. U.S. kindergarten MMR coverage stood at 95.2 percent in the 2019–2020 school year, fell to 92.5 percent by 2024–2025, and stands at 92.4 percent in 2025–2026. Pennsylvania’s kindergarten rate was 93.2 percent last year; school coverage in Spartanburg County fell from 95 percent to under 89 percent over a decade; Mohave County, Arizona, which includes Colorado City, reported 78.4 percent in 2024. In southern Alberta, reporting from the outbreak period put two-dose coverage among children at about 56 percent. More than 90 percent of U.S. cases in 2026 have been in people unvaccinated or of unknown status. Mexico’s gap has its own history: the measles vaccine reached Mexico years after the 1963 U.S. licensure, and health officials there have described both vaccine shortages in recent years and complacency in a generation that no longer saw measles.

The CDC issued an alert this week reporting 112 confirmed measles infections during pregnancy in the United States from January 2025 through September 2026, nearly all in women unvaccinated or of unknown status, and 13 cases of congenital measles, transmitted to the infant before birth, the first such cluster reported in the country in decades. The MMR vaccine cannot be given during pregnancy.

5. The Policy Argument in the United States

The U.S. resurgence has become an argument about the Secretary of Health and Human Services, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who led Children’s Health Defense, an organization critical of federal vaccine policy, before taking office. The record of his statements runs in both directions. In April 2025 he wrote that “the most effective way to prevent the spread of measles is the MMR vaccine,” a post that drew anger from anti-vaccine activists. In the same period he called the vaccine “leaky” and said it had not been safety tested, a claim reporters and fact-checkers have called false. In 2021, before taking office, he told an Amish audience on a Lancaster County farm that health authorities wanted them vaccinated because they could not stand that the Amish were healthy. Across seven congressional hearings in April 2026 he said the department promotes the vaccine, said he had never been anti-vaccine, and declined to accept responsibility for the outbreaks; he has repeatedly said the United States is controlling measles better than any other country, a claim FactCheck.org found faulty. Senator Raphael Warnock and other Democrats have called for his removal. Federal officials, Kennedy among them, now describe vaccination as the best protection, and the CDC continues to recommend two doses. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said this month that the loss of elimination status would not change the agency’s approach.

The comparative record bears on the argument from both sides. Public-health critics point to declining trust in federal health messaging and to the weaker response in Texas in 2025 compared with New York in 2019. The same record shows Canada losing its status first, a year ahead of the United States; Mexico and Bolivia losing theirs alongside the United States; Guatemala carrying the hemisphere’s largest outbreak; and the decline in U.S. kindergarten coverage beginning in the 2019–2020 school year, during the pandemic disruption of routine childhood care. PAHO’s own explanation for the regional resurgence names immunity gaps in specific communities and geographic areas, barriers to health services, missed vaccinations, misinformation, and hesitancy, and it names no government.

6. What Losing Elimination Status Means

Elimination is a finding about transmission. It never meant zero cases; it meant measles could enter a country but could not sustain a chain of its own for a year. Losing it reclassifies the country as endemic and changes no law or treaty. Barbosa called the loss “a serious warning” and said it is not irreversible; elimination, in his phrase, is not a trophy won once and placed on a shelf. To regain the status, each country must interrupt its chain and then document twelve months without endemic transmission. Canada has interrupted its chain and is now working toward reverification. Mexico’s health authorities have said the national outbreak may be nearing its end.

7. What the Record Does Not Settle

The record establishes the chain’s early route through related Mennonite communities in Canada, Texas, and Chihuahua by sequencing and case investigation. It does not establish the full route of every later outbreak; the Spartanburg outbreak’s initial source is unknown, and PAHO’s spring report identified the D8 lineage across at least ten countries without assigning lineage to each. Case counts are confirmed counts and are undercounts by the agencies’ own statements, with Guatemala’s figure shaped by a change in its confirmation method. The record does not apportion the U.S. decline in coverage among the pandemic’s disruption of routine care, changes in public trust, federal messaging, and local exemption law, and no study on the shelf has done so. The cocked hat is printed as found: one lineage, carried first through close-knit communities linked by family and migration across three borders, then into the general and Indigenous populations of the countries it reached.

 The Filed Clippings

 Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective, a source with a position, printed because it is useful, and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only part of this file stamped objective. Fourteen items.

 

 SubjectivePan American Health Organization—“PAHO urges countries to step up efforts to stop measles outbreaks and move towards elimination in the Americas” (November 17, 2026)The decision itself: Bolivia, Mexico, and the United States lose elimination status after the commission’s November 10–13 meeting; the twelve-month genotype-and-lineage test; 58,213 confirmed cases and 82 deaths in the region in 2026 as of November 13; Canada’s interrupted chain; and the Director’s statements that the loss is serious and reversible.

 SubjectiveThe Hill—“US loses measles elimination status after more than 25 years” (November 17, 2026)The briefing as reported in Washington: the Director’s acceptance of the commission’s recommendation for all three countries, and more than 7,700 U.S. cases across two years with more than ten state-reported deaths.

 SubjectivePan American Health Organization—“Ten countries in the Americas report measles outbreaks in 2025” (August 15, 2025)The genotype finding: one genotype across eight countries, particularly among Mennonite communities; 71 percent of cases unvaccinated and 18 percent unknown; Indigenous communities hardest hit in Mexico, with a case-fatality rate about twenty times the general population’s; and an early note that cases were rising outside these groups.
